headline: Adopted a data center zoning change, approved a liquor license and legal retainer, and advanced the sale of 12 Water Street and a labor contract.
summary: Councilors also adopted a highway safety grant and a drainage easement at 41 Brown Street. The 12 Water Street sale and the labor contract each still need a second reading.
decisions: Adopted Orders 2026-118 and 2026-119 on second and final reading, 6-0.
Adopted Order 2026-120, amending the land use ordinance regarding data centers, 6-0.
Approved a liquor license for Sweet Caroline's Retro Lounge, 6-0.
Adopted Order 2026-121, authorizing a legal retainer agreement for fire apparatus antitrust litigation, 6-0.
Passed the first of two readings of Order 2026-122 to authorize the sale of 12 Water Street, by a show of hands with none opposed.
Passed the first of two readings of Order 2026-123 approving the 2026-2029 collective bargaining agreement with the Westbrook Essential Services Unit, by a show of hands with none opposed.

WESTBROOK CITY COUNCIL 
REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 
MONDAY, NOVEMBER 2, 2026 AT 6:00 PM  
WESTBROOK HIGH SCHOOL (ROOM 114) 
125 STROUDWATER ST.  
 
 
 
  
I. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT 
Meeting called to order at 6:00pm by City Council President Jennifer Munro. President Munro stated a 
reminder of the City Council Rules of Order regarding meeting conduct. City Clerk Ellis Ledoux read the City 
Council Land Acknowledgment statement into the record. 
 
  
II. ROLL CALL 
City Councilors Present: Brian McCambridge (Ward 1), Anna A. Turcotte (Ward 3), Victor Chau (Ward 2), Amy 
Faulkingham (Ward 4), Jennifer Munro (Ward 5, President), Gary Rairdon (At-Large) 
 
City Councilors Absent: Michael Shaughnessy (At-Large, Vice President) 
 
Other City Officials Present: Eric Dudley (Director of Engineering & Public Services), Jennie Franceschi 
(Assistant City Administrator), Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Ellis Ledoux (City Clerk), Joanne LePauloue 
(Director of Human Resources), David Morse (Mayor), Monique Cornett (Director of Economic Development), 
Cameron Ferrante (Legal Counsel), Bruno Inacio (Finance Director), Rebecca Spitella (Director of Planning & 
Code Enforcement),Gary Wagner (Assistant Fire Chief) 
 
  
III. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
City Council President Munro led all present in the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
  
IV. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
No minutes were presented for approval. 
 
  
V. MAYOR'S MESSAGE  
 
 Mayor Morse read his message into the record. A summary is included below: 
• Mayor Morse invited Glenn Fenton, Executive Director of METRO to present METRO's 2027 
Budget & Municipal Assessment. The following Councilors spoke: Councilor Rairdon, Councilor 
Chau, President Munro, Councilor McCambridge, Mayor Morse 
• Robyn Saunders will provide an overview of the Landslide Vulnerability Assessment at the next 
City Council Meeting held on November 16, 2026 
• Encourage residents to attend the Main St. redesign on November 13th at Westbrook Warren 
Congregational Church with the City of Westbrook and MaineDOT.  
•  Election Day is tomorrow at the Westbrook Community Center. Voting will be open from 6am-
8pm.
VI. CITY COUNCIL MESSAGES 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for City Council messages. Councilors provided the following 
updates: 
• Councilor Rairdon promoted "Stuff A Bus" in the Hannaford parking lot on the following weekends: 
Saturday & Sunday, November 7th -8th, and November 14th& 15th.  
• Councilor Chau thanked the Westbrook Marching Band. They performed at Harvard and got 2nd place 
• Councilor Turcotte mentioned it was amazing to see them perform against all Massachusetts schools. 
Congratulations to them and the music staff.  
 
  
VII. STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE UPDATE 
There was no Student Representative update. 
 
  
VIII. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the first public comment portion of this meeting. The 
following individuals spoke: Larry McWilliams (Westbrook Resident), Matthew Brunner (Westbrook Resident) 
 
 
  
IX. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
There was no unfinished business for consideration.  
 
  
X. ORDERS OF THE DAY (SECOND AND FINAL READING)  
 
 Order 2026-118. Authorizing Acceptance & Expenditure of Bureau of Highway Safety Grant Funds  
Order 2026-119. Authorizing a Drainage Easement at 41 Brown Street 
 Motion to approve second and final reading of Orders 2026-118 & 2026-119 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro asked if any Councilor would like to consider any item separately. No one 
spoke 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: No one spoke. 
Motion carried. Order 2026-118 & 2026-119 adopted. (Vote 6-0) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy 
 
 
 
 
 Order 2026-120. Amending the Land Use Ordinance Regarding Data Centers  
 A public hearing on this item was held. Notice of the public hearing was published in the Portland Press 
Herald on Friday, October 23rd, posted to the City of Westbrook's website, and was posted in City Hall. 
 
City Council President Munro opened the public hearing. The following individuals spoke: No one 
spoke.
City Council President Munro closed the public hearing. 
Motion to approve second and final reading of Order 2026-120 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Mayor Morse  
Motion carried. Order 2026-120 adopted. (Vote 6-0) 
Ayes:  McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy 
 
  
XI. NEW BUSINESS  
 
  
 Business Licenses  
 
 Liquor License for Sweet Caroline's Retro Lounge (1 Westbrook Common, Suite 5)  
 A public hearing on this item was held. Notice of the public hearing was published in the Portland Press 
Herald on Friday, October 23rd, posted to the City of Westbrook's website, and was posted in City Hall. 
 
City Council President Munro opened the public hearing. The following individuals spoke: Caroline 
Donovan (Owner of Sweet Caroline's Retro Lounge) 
City Council President Munro closed the public hearing. 
 
Motion to approve liquor license 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Councilor Rairdon 
Motion carried. Liquor License approved (Vote 6-0) 
Ayes: McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy 
 
 
 
  
 Orders (One Reading Required)  
 
 Order 2026-121. Authorizing Retainer Agreement for Legal Representation in Fire Apparatus 
Antitrust Litigation  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation.  
Moved by Councilor McCambridge, seconded by Councilor Rairdon 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator) 
Motion carried. Order 2026-121 adopted. (Vote 6-0) 
Ayes: McCambridge, Chau, Turcotte, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy
Orders (Two Readings Required) 
Order 2026-122. Authorizing Sale of 12 Water Street  
Motion to approve the first of two readings of the legislation. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: City Administrator Holmes, Councilor Rairdon, Andrew Broaddus (Legal Representative for Ms. 
Schulburger), Alice Peterson (Resident of Westbrook), Larry McWilliams (Westbrook Resident) 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed. 
Order 2026-123. Approving the 2026-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement with the Westbrook 
Essential Services Unit  
Motion to approve the first of two readings of the legislation. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor McCambridge 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator) 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed. 
XII. PUBLIC COMMENT
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the second and final public comment portion of this 
meeting. The following individuals spoke: Ken Foassen (Westbrook resident), Marc Fournier (Westbrook 
Resident)
XIII. REFERRALS
There were no referrals for consideration.
XIV. COMMITTEE REPORTS
The following items remain in their City Council Committees for deliberation. No updates were provided 
by Committee Chairs.
Committee of the Whole
Board, Commission, Committee Ordinance
Code of Conduct & Job Descriptions for Elected Officials
Private Ways Ordinance
Facilities & Streets Committee
Establishment of Memorial Area
Policy on Establishing Memorial Areas
Friends of Warren Recreational Area Introductions & Updates
Haskell Street Traffic Calming
Housing & Economic Development Committee 
Cannabis Dispensary Zoning Regulations  
  
XV. EXECUTIVE SESSION  
 
 Request to enter into Executive Session pursuant to 1 M.R.S.A. Section 405-6(E) for consultation with 
the City Solicitor concerning the legal rights and duties of the City, inviting the following individuals 
to attend: City Solicitor. 
 Motion to enter into Executive Session as stated above. 
Moved by Chau, seconded by Rairdon. 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed.  
 
  
XVI. ADJOURNMENT 
Motion to adjourn at 7:42pm 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor Faulkingham 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed.
